newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt court to try teenaged militant for violence.
newsitem.headline: Egypt court to try teenaged militant for violence.

text.p: A suspected Moslem militant will go on trial in an Egyptian state security court on Tuesday charged with killing five policemen and two civilians when he was 14 years old, security sources said on Monday.
They said Mohammed Ali el-Badri, 18, could face a sentence ranging from three to 25 years with hard labour if he is found guilty of the charges.

Badri is being charged under a new law that allows the trial and imprisonment of suspected militants who are less than 18 years old. Previously, under-aged militants would be tried in juvenile courts and sent to a home for young offenders.
Police arrested Badri earlier this year in the southern province of Assiut where he is accused of killing the policemen and civilians in 1994.

Badri is also being tried in another case in a state security court, along with 32 other suspected militants, on charges of trying to overthrow the government, killing 26 policemen and carrying out several other violent attacks, the sources said.
He is being tried as an adult in that case although he was less than 18 years old when he allegedly took part in the crimes, the sources said.
They said he could face the death sentence if found guilty of the charges in the second trial.
Moslem militants launched a bloody campaign in 1992 to overthrow the government and set up a strict Islamic state.
More than 1,000 people, mainly militants and policemen, have been killed in political violence since then.
